newsitem.title: USA: Rexene says board backed by ISS.
newsitem.headline: Rexene says board backed by ISS.

text.p: Rexene Corp said in a statement that proxy advisory Institutional Shareholder Services Inc has recommended shareholders reject the attempt by a group of shareholders led by Wyser-Pratte & Co Inc and Spear Leeds & Kellogg to replace Rexene's board.
""The dissidents charge that current management has done nothing to enhance shareholder value ... ISS fails to see this," Rexene quoted the report as saying.
There will be a shareholder meeting on April 30 at which the dissidents will attempt to overthrow the board.

"Since 1993, the company has gone from negative net worth to more than $170 million in shareholders' equity ... and a $2.40 loss per share is now $1.55 per share in earnings," Rexene quoted the report as saying.

Rexene said that ISS had also backed its demands that privately held Huntsman Corp should demonstrate its ability to finance a deal for Rexene and should agree to be bound by confidentiality clauses if it wants to make a bid.
Huntsman has said that it is interested in acquiring Rexene, but it will not deal with the current management.

Discussing the company's proposed stock repurchase program, Rexene quoted ISS as saying, "We believe a repurchase offers the benefits of cashing out at a premium price or remaining invested with a boost to earnings per share and to the stock price. As outlined by Rexene, there is no provision in the preferred share issuance that would obstruct a potential acquirer." ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
